needs_review: Interval notation: validation ranks are written as bracket pairs such as [2048, 2560] (configs/p5_hierarchy_ablation.toml:27; results/p5-2026-11-13/b101-o301-baseline/config.resolved.json "validation_ranks"). Read as half-open, the meaning is ranks 2048..2559, which is what the code slices (src/arborlm/p5_data.py:26, 49-50, 58-59) and the ADR prose (ADR-0010 line 79; ADR-0013 line 53) state. The brackets alone do not show whether 2560 is excluded. If the brackets were read as closed, rank 2560 would appear in the P5, P6-Q and P7-A evaluations, and the item-3 answer would change. The lead should confirm the convention. This inventory does not resolve it.

P1 validation range [0, 512) and training consumption [0, 2048) are not written as rank intervals in any P1 record. They are derived from configs/p1_ram_screen.toml:11-12, src/arborlm/pilot_data.py:80 (ranked[:count]), src/arborlm/pilot_config.py:23 and src/arborlm/pilot.py:242. The training-consumption figure is a derivation from the step and batch arithmetic, not a recorded statement.

The memory diagnostic's validation range is not stated as a rank interval in its own records. It reuses the P1 frozen validation file (ADR-0006 line 10; validation.bytes SHA-256 2e6b71b9… is identical to P1), so [0, 512) is inherited by reference.

P6-E records (results/p6-e-2026-11-13/ and experiments/P6EANA-, P6ECON-, P6EEQ-, P6ESCR-) contain no validation rank interval and no panel SHA-256. The P5 panel identity for P6-E comes only from ADR-0011 (line 42) and the module docstring src/arborlm/p6_equivalence.py lines 1-5.

P7-A records give the evaluation and calibration ranks ([2048,2560]) in the trace checkpoint JSON but no panel SHA-256. The P5 panel hash d50cbe4c… appears in P6-Q and P5 records only. The P7-A panel identity is stated in ADR-0013 line 53 and docs/reviews/p7a-preflight-2026-11-13/AUDIT.md line 110, which give no hash.
